facts.topic: DAG construction
facts.detail: Dag.__init__(roots) calls _add(expr) per root; _add recurses into expr.operands, dedups purely on the structural key() string via self.by_key, and records which root positions point to each shared Node in node.root_indices. topo is children-before-parents post-order.

facts.topic: CSE key format
facts.detail: key() is cached on the Expression (_key slot) and is a pure structural string with no view/store identity in it: Feature='F:{field}', Constant='C:{value!r}', _OpNode='O:{spec.name}(child1.key(),...)|w{window}', GeneralCall='G:{spec.name}(...)'.

facts.topic: is_leaf is the only leaf-type check in the DAG
facts.detail: Node.is_leaf = isinstance(self.expr, (Feature, Constant)) — a hardcoded 2-type tuple. Dag.computed = every node NOT is_leaf; leaves get no mode/round_id and are excluded from assign_modes/plan_rounds entirely ('leaves are never scheduled').

facts.topic: Exhaustive list of is_leaf / leaf-type consumers
facts.detail: Grep-verified: dag.py:40 (definition), dag.py:76 (Dag.computed), schedule.py:62 (_p_eligible), schedule.py:84 (assign_modes step 2 skips leaf children), schedule.py:113 (closure() readiness — a leaf is always 'ready'), engine.py:192 (bare-leaf-root path), engine.py:278 (_run_cube_chunk.operand). engine.py:357 (_run_panel_round.operand) has NO is_leaf check at all — it only special-cases Constant. No occurrence of is_leaf or Feature/Constant isinstance checks anywhere in kernels.py.

facts.topic: assign_modes algorithm
facts.detail: 3 passes over dag.computed: (1) hard requirement + P-eligibility bottom-up via _p_eligible; (2) free nodes inherit mode from computed cube children bottom-up (leaf children explicitly skipped here); (3) else inherit from parents top-down, else default 'S'.

facts.topic: _p_eligible
facts.detail: A node can run in panel (P) mode if spec.face=='nd' (always), or if family=='elementwise' and every child is (is_leaf AND shape.degenerate) or (not is_leaf AND (mode==MODE_P OR shape.degenerate)). Today the leaf branch is only ever exercised by Constant, since Feature.shape.degenerate is always False.

facts.topic: plan_rounds / round formation
facts.detail: Greedy: repeatedly compute closure(MODE_P) first (free), else whichever of closure(MODE_S)/closure(MODE_D) is larger; each chosen node gets round_id=len(rounds). After all rounds exist, per-node boundary/panel_out/bound_layout/mask_out are derived by comparing round_id across parent edges: cross-round + degenerate -> panel_out (in-memory (S,D) hand-off); cross-round + full-width -> boundary (on-disk memmap); a boundary read ONLY by D-mode rounds is stored day-major for I/O locality; mask_out marks where the NaN mask must be re-applied under the default 'boundaries' policy (roots, panel_out, boundary, or any node feeding a D-axis/S-axis/NT op).

facts.topic: Face/compute-axis type table (why cross_* needs full D, nt_cs_* needs full S)
facts.detail: The canonical table: dt/in,day are M-axis (chunkable on S or D); dt/cross is D-axis, chunkable only on S (needs the whole day axis per stock); nd/cs,ts are whole-panel (D,S), never chunked; nt/cs,ts are per-day (M,S) face calls, D-mode only. OpSpec.allowed_modes encodes this directly: face=='nd'->(P,); face=='nt'->(D,); compute_axis=='D'->(S,) [cross_*]; compute_axis=='S'->(D,) [nt_cs_*].

facts.topic: evaluate() top-level flow
facts.detail: Validates every root is shape.degenerate (raises unless tolerant=True, collecting per-index errors instead); builds Dag+plan_rounds; computes (cs,cd) via _chunk_sizes; for a MODE_P round calls _run_panel_round ONCE on whole (D,S) tensors (no chunk loop); for S/D rounds, loops lo in range(0,n,step) with step=cs|cd and n=S|D, calling _run_cube_chunk per chunk.

facts.topic: _chunk_sizes byte-budget model
facts.detail: wmax = largest .window among computed nodes that are not restores_m; overhead=12+min(wmax,64); per_symbol=D*M*4*overhead bytes, per_day=S*M*4*overhead; cs/cd = explicit chunk_symbols/chunk_days if given, else chunk_bytes // per_symbol_or_day clamped to [1,S or D]. chunk_bytes defaults to 2<<30 (2 GiB). The model scales purely with M (minute width); it has no notion of a leaf that is only (C,D) or (S,C).

facts.topic: _load_leaf_cube is the sole in-chunk leaf reader, and it is NOT isinstance(Feature)-gated
facts.detail: Constant -> torch.full((1,1,1), expr.value, dtype=self.dtype, device=self.device) built directly in the engine's configured dtype. Anything else (today always a Feature) falls through unconditionally to arr = view.read_s(expr.field,lo,hi) or view.read_d(expr.field,lo,hi), i.e. it assumes a '.field' attribute and a (C,D,M)/(S,C,M) cube on disk, with no isinstance(Feature) check at all. The result is then masked via self._mask_cube(t, tradable).

facts.topic: Feature leaves are always read from disk as float32, Constant is built directly in engine dtype
facts.detail: CubeStore.read_cube and SegmentedCubeStore.read_cube both hardcode dtype=np.float32 for the numpy array; .to(self.device,self.dtype) upcasts to float64 only afterward if dtype='float64'. Constant's torch.full(...) is built directly in self.dtype, skipping the float32 round-trip. A new leaf type that is NOT backed by a float32 numpy source would need to decide which path it follows.

facts.topic: Bare-leaf-as-root path has a leaf-type gap of its own
facts.detail: evaluate()'s final output-collection loop special-cases node.is_leaf -> self._leaf_panel(node.expr); _leaf_panel handles ONLY Constant and otherwise raises ValueError(f'leaf {expr!r} is not a daily value') — the error text itself already names the exact concept ('a daily value') that a new leaf type would need to satisfy.

facts.topic: P-round operand loader has NO fallback for any leaf besides Constant
facts.detail: _run_panel_round.operand() special-cases isinstance(c.expr, Constant) (-> torch.full((1,1),...)), else only looks in `values` (same-round already-computed) or `panels` (hand-off from an earlier round); any other leaf type raises RuntimeError('panel operand {key} unavailable'). This path is never hit today because Feature is never P-eligible, but a new leaf marked shape.degenerate=True WILL be routed into P-mode by _p_eligible for the common elementwise case (e.g. div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap)), making this the first real gap most new-leaf designs will hit.

facts.topic: Collapsed intermediate stitching across S/D chunks
facts.detail: On n.panel_out, panels[n.key] is lazily allocated once as np.full((S,D),nan); each chunk takes out[...,0] (column 0, exact for a degenerate value), expands a fully-collapsed (1,1) chunk result up to the chunk's real stock/day extent, masks it, then writes into the disjoint slice p[lo:hi,:] (S-mode) or p[:,lo:hi] (D-mode). Chunks within a round are processed strictly sequentially and never overlap, so stitching is just writing into disjoint slices of one persistent array — no merge/reduce step exists or is needed.

facts.topic: Full-width (boundary) stitching across a mode switch
facts.detail: On n.boundary, a np.memmap is lazily created under a per-call TemporaryDirectory, shaped (D,S,width) or (S,D,width) per n.bound_layout (width comes from the actual result's last dim, e.g. narrower after in_slice); each chunk writes its slice, transposed when the writing round's axis order differs from the file's stored layout. Cleaned up (tmp.cleanup()) at the end of every evaluate() call — never persisted.

facts.topic: Internal panel orientation differs from the external result orientation
facts.detail: The internal `panels` dict is (S,D) float32 ('key -> (S,D) float32'); EvalResult.panels (user-facing) is (D,S), produced by one final transpose per root at the very end of evaluate() (out[i]=np.ascontiguousarray(p.T,...)). A new daily-leaf's raw data is described by the task as already '(D,S)' — that is the OPPOSITE of the engine's own internal (S,D) convention, so a transpose decision point exists wherever the new leaf's raw array is first touched.

facts.topic: Per-chunk operand memoization and eviction
facts.detail: _run_cube_chunk.operand() caches each distinct child's tensor by c.key in a per-chunk `values` dict (checked before is_leaf/panels/bounds), guaranteeing one store-read (or one panel/boundary slice) per distinct operand per chunk regardless of how many trees reference it; evicted via a remaining_uses refcount once the last use within the round is spent, except when c.is_root (reason for that specific exemption not established with certainty from reading the code — see open_questions). This CSE-at-read-time behavior is locked by test_each_operand_is_read_once_per_chunk.

facts.topic: kernels.py never inspects leaf type
facts.detail: apply_cube/apply_panel operate purely on already-loaded tensors, dispatching only on spec.face/compute_axis/family; grep confirms zero references to Feature/Constant/is_leaf anywhere in kernels.py. M-axis ops get a zero-copy (A*B,M) row view, NT ops loop per day over a (M,S) face, D-axis (cross_*) ops loop per stock over (D,M) restricted to mode==MODE_S (raises RuntimeError otherwise), elementwise uses plain torch broadcasting. Consequence: a new leaf TYPE needs zero kernels.py changes — the change is entirely in 'how a leaf becomes a tensor', not in 'what an operator does with a tensor'.

facts.topic: _align_widths / width-1 broadcasting
facts.detail: _align_widths broadcasts any width-1 operand up to the shared minute width and explicitly raises ValueError on two genuinely different non-1 widths. A degenerate leaf naturally presents as width-1 here, the same path Constant already uses — no special-casing needed once the tensor shape is right.

facts.topic: CubeView construction and the private _rows helper
facts.detail: CubeView(store, sym_idx, d0, d1) precomputes self._contiguous (whether sym_idx is one ascending run) once in __init__; _rows(s_lo,s_hi) returns a cheap contiguous slice when possible, else an explicit fancy-index array. read_s/read_d BOTH delegate symbol-index resolution to _rows and day-index resolution to self.d0+lo offsetting.

facts.topic: read_s / read_d contracts
facts.detail: read_s(name,s_lo,s_hi) -> (C,D,M) float32 for view-local symbols [s_lo,s_hi), full view day range, via store.read_cube(name, self._rows(s_lo,s_hi), self.d0, self.d1). read_d(name,d_lo,d_hi) -> (S,C,M) float32 for view-local days [d_lo,d_hi), full view symbol set, via store.read_cube(name, self._rows(0,n_symbols), self.d0+d_lo, self.d0+d_hi).

facts.topic: tradable() is the existing precedent for a whole-view-cached, thinly-sliced (S,D) accessor
facts.detail: CubeView.tradable() computes and caches a (S,D) bool for the WHOLE view exactly once (store.read_status + np.isin against TRADING/RESUMED codes, cached in self._tradable); tradable_s/tradable_d are thin lo:hi slices of that cached array. This is structurally the closest existing template for a new daily-field accessor: compute/cache the whole-view (S,D) array once, then slice.

facts.topic: CubeStore's on-disk format structurally assumes one shared (S,D,M) shape across all fields in a store
facts.detail: build_cube_store requires `len({cubes[n].shape for n in names}) == 1` (all fields share one (S,D,M) shape); CubeStore.field() separately asserts `arr.shape == (n_symbols,n_days,n_minutes)` per field. A daily (S,D) field cannot simply be added as an 'M=1' entry inside the SAME store directory without changing one of these checks (or writing it as a genuinely separate store/format). store.py's own module docstring states 'There is no separate daily store: daily fields are cube expressions' — referring to the PRE-EXISTING day_last(Close)-style derived values, not to new exogenous daily data.

facts.topic: CubeStore field-level caching and mirror/madvise machinery exists because minute cubes are gigabytes
facts.detail: CubeStore.field() mmaps and caches dtfield_<name>.npy per field name, shared across every CubeView built from that store. read_cube additionally picks a D-major 'mirror' when the slice pattern is few-days/many-symbols, driven by advise_access madvise hints — documented as mattering because a strided read without the hint pulled ~197x the wanted bytes on a 9.8 GB field. A (S,D) daily field at the SAME production scale (5219 symbols x 1942 days x 4 bytes) is only ~40 MB per field, small enough to load wholesale into RAM with ordinary numpy indexing, so none of this mmap/madvise/mirror machinery is a hard requirement for daily fields.

facts.topic: SegmentedCubeStore joins an immutable base with append-only date segments
facts.detail: SegmentedCubeStore combines `<root>/minute` (base) with `<root>/incremental/<rel>/minute` segments listed in `incremental/index.json`; read_cube/read_status fan a requested slice across whichever segments cover the requested days and reassemble into one array, filling any uncovered cell with NaN. Whether daily fields need an analogous incremental-append story, or can be rebuilt wholesale, is not established (open question).

facts.topic: The engine has NO concept of warm-up; it is 100% caller-side convention
facts.detail: view.n_days always spans the engine's full evaluation window with no padding/trim logic inside CubeEngine or CubeView. research.warmed_view(store,start,end,warmup,...) extends the view's d0 backward by `warmup` raw day-index positions and returns (CubeView, trim) where trim=base.d0-d0; downstream code (pipeline.run_mining, fullcatalog.evaluate_factors) explicitly slices result[trim:] after evaluate() to drop the padded rows. expression.max_window(expr,'D') (largest rolling-window literal along the day axis in a tree) is how callers size how much warm-up a given expression set actually needs.

facts.topic: cross_* day-axis rolling NaN-pads at the start of whatever day span it is given
facts.detail: operators/common.py's rolling_windows(x,d,axis) left-pads axis with d-1 NaNs then unfolds — causal, no wraparound. Because cross_* (compute_axis='D') is restricted to allowed_modes=(MODE_S,), an S-mode chunk always carries the FULL view day axis (chunking is only over stocks in S-mode), so this NaN-pad happens exactly once, at the start of the VIEW's day range, not per day-chunk. Correctness for the 'real' analysis window depends entirely on the caller having padded the view's d0 far enough back via warmed_view.

facts.topic: UniverseEngine is a pure post-hoc decorator on EvalResult.panels
facts.detail: UniverseEngine.evaluate() calls through to the wrapped engine unchanged, then overwrites every output panel with np.where(self._member, p, np.nan); __getattr__ forwards every other attribute/method (including .view) straight to the wrapped engine. It never touches leaf-loading, chunking, or the panels/bounds dicts internal to CubeEngine.evaluate() — zero changes needed here for a new daily leaf.

facts.topic: UniverseEngine is constructed at two separate call sites
facts.detail: run_mining wraps the shared `engine` once (for non-GP miners/labels), and separately re-wraps GPMiner's OWN internally-constructed engine (with an explicit comment that GP builds its own engine so it must be wrapped again). Any change to how CubeEngine is constructed (e.g. passing new daily-field data) must be threaded through both sites.

facts.topic: Device plumbing is uniform; no device-conditional code exists in engine.py/kernels.py
facts.detail: CubeEngine.__init__ sets self.device=torch.device(device) (default 'cpu') and self.dtype; every tensor the engine creates is moved via .to(self.device,self.dtype) at each of 9+ call sites (leaves, panel-slices, boundary-slices, constants, masking). torch_threads, if given, calls the GLOBAL torch.set_num_threads(...) — a process-wide side effect, not scoped to one engine instance.

facts.topic: There is no dedicated OOM-handling code in engine.py/kernels.py/store.py/dag.py/schedule.py
facts.detail: Grep across all 5 assigned files for OOM/cuda/OutOfMemory/MemoryError finds nothing beyond ordinary device plumbing. The ONLY exception handling in the chunk/panel evaluation loops is the generic `except Exception as exc:` in _run_cube_chunk and _run_panel_round, active only under evaluate(tolerant=True); it sets n.failed/n.error and lets any dependent node (checked at the top of each node's processing) also fail and be skipped, rather than raising. A CUDA OutOfMemoryError is caught by this SAME generic path with no type-specific handling.

facts.topic: The actual GPU memory cap and the 'OOM is silent' design intent live in cli.py / mining/, outside the 5 assigned files
facts.detail: cli.py reads env var ALPHACUBE_GPU_FRACTION and calls torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(frac) when device starts with 'cuda', with an explicit comment: tolerant-mode engine OOM 'only lets the node silently fail, no error is raised'. mining/gp.py and mining/env.py each have their own comments explicitly relying on this contract (CUDA OOM in the tolerant engine drops the tree silently) to batch large exemplar evaluations without crashing the run.

facts.topic: Test fixtures build real on-disk synthetic stores, session-scoped
facts.detail: tests/conftest.py: `registry` = catalog.default_registry(); `store` = synthetic.write_synthetic_store(root, n_symbols=10, n_days=60, n_minutes=24, seed=11, suspended_frac=0.05, unlisted_days=8); `view` = store.view(); `raw` = an independent {field:(S,D,M)} + tradable-masked reference copy read directly off store.field(f), bypassing CubeView, used as ground truth in test_engine.py.

facts.topic: synthetic.py builds realistic in-memory cubes then writes the real on-disk format
facts.detail: make_synthetic_cube builds Open/High/Low/Close/Volume/Vwap/Ret/Amt with common-factor+idiosyncratic-walk closes, a Brownian-bridge intraday path, U-shaped volume, an optional planted day_std(Ret)->next-day-return signal (plant_beta), random SUSPENDED stock-days (suspended_frac), and an OUTSIDE_LIFECYCLE tail on the last symbol (unlisted_days); write_synthetic_store then calls store.build_cube_store to write the genuine dt_meta.json + dtfield_*.npy + day_status.npy layout, so tests exercise the real CubeStore disk-read path, not a mock.

facts.topic: test_engine.py correctness/chunk-invariance strategy
facts.detail: References are computed by looping per-symbol or per-day calls directly into alphacube.operators.* (never through the engine), e.g. test_dt_families_bit_exact_vs_per_symbol. Chunk-invariance is pinned by running the same expressions under several (chunk_symbols,chunk_days) pairs including degenerate (1,1) and asserting bit-exact equality against the unchunked default, both on a fixed small set (test_chunk_invariance) and on a random TypedTreeGenerator population covering every registered operator (test_chunk_invariance_over_random_population). test_kernels_never_write_into_operands builds ONE expression per registry.list_all() entry (so any newly-registered operator — or, by extension, a working new leaf type used in such an expression — is automatically swept in) against a private n_minutes=241 synthetic store.

facts.topic: Boundary/mode-switch tests pin the exact disk layout and read/write access pattern
facts.detail: test_boundary_materialisation, test_boundary_reads_and_writes_follow_the_access_pattern, and test_day_major_boundaries_give_the_same_values construct cross_*/nt_cs_* combinations that force S<->D mode switches and assert on plan.boundaries, eng._bound_layout, and (via monkeypatching advise_access) the exact sequence of strided-vs-contiguous madvise calls.

facts.topic: test_device_parity.py scope and skip condition
facts.detail: Accelerator-specific tests (needs_accel) skip entirely when neither torch.cuda.is_available() nor torch.backends.mps.is_available(). What is unconditionally tested regardless of hardware is the dtype='float64' reference-widening mode, used as the arbiter for float32-vs-accelerator comparisons since cross-device float32 reduction order is explicitly NOT promised — only the finite/NaN pattern and bit-exactness of selection operators (day_last etc., which pick rather than reduce) are required to match across devices. No OOM-specific test exists in this file or in test_engine.py.

facts.topic: CubeView itself has direct unit coverage, independent of the engine
facts.detail: test_store.py::test_view_selection_and_reads exercises read_s/read_d against both a contiguous max_symbols/date-range view and a non-contiguous explicit-symbols view (checking fancy-indexing correctness and that the returned array is independently writeable); test_tradable_matches_status checks tradable() against the day_status plane directly.

facts.topic: Parsing: a bare identifier becomes Feature(field) in exactly one place, gated by a hardcoded field tuple
facts.detail: catalog.CUBE_FIELDS=('Open','High','Low','Close','Volume','Vwap','Ret','Amt') is a hardcoded, store-independent tuple fed into Registry(fields=...) via build_registry/default_registry. parser._Parser.name(ident) is the ONLY place a bare identifier becomes Feature(field), gated by `ident in self.reg.fields` (==CUBE_FIELDS) or FIELD_ALIASES; an unrecognized identifier (e.g. 'FloatCap' today) raises ParseError unless it also matches DAILY_MACROS/DAILY_NAME_ALIASES, both of which expand to ordinary MINUTE-cube expressions (e.g. close_1d -> day_last(Close)), not to a new exogenous value.

facts.topic: daily.py's 'daily' concept is a DIFFERENT, pre-existing mechanism and must not be conflated with the task's new exogenous daily fields
facts.detail: daily.py's DailyData/DAILY_FIELD_EXPRESSIONS table maps every daily field name to a cube-expression STRING (e.g. 'Close':'day_last(Close)') evaluated by the engine from the real minute cube; the module docstring explicitly says it 'is never a data source'. FloatCap/TotalCap/etc. have no minute-cube representation at all and cannot be produced by any day_* expression over an existing Feature, so they are a genuinely new kind of leaf, not an instance of this existing mechanism.

facts.topic: Within one evaluate() call, every engine-internal cache is keyed purely by structural expr.key(), with no view identity, and is discarded at the end of the call
facts.detail: `values` (per-chunk), `panels`, and `bounds` are all local variables of CubeEngine.evaluate(), keyed by node.key; bounds.clear() and tmp.cleanup() run in evaluate()'s finally block. There is NO cross-call panel cache anywhere in engine.py/dag.py/schedule.py/kernels.py — a brand-new CubeEngine/Dag is built on every evaluate() call.

facts.topic: A SEPARATE, higher-level panel cache exists outside the assigned files (located but not read in depth)
facts.detail: mining/gp.py and mining/env.py each keep their own `self._panel_cache` (ctor params panel_cache_items/panel_cache_bytes). mining/rankban.py::view_cache_key(view,sample_days,sample_symbols) fingerprints a VIEW (not an expression) by hashing (first_date,last_date,n_dates,n_symbols,sample_days,sample_symbols) — for a different cache (ExemplarCache). This is the closest existing precedent for 'view identity' as a cache-key component that the task's own prompt worries about ('面板缓存的键要正确'), but these files are outside my assigned scope (engine/ + store.py CubeView) and were only located by grep, not read.

insertion_points.change: Add the new daily-leaf Expression class to the isinstance tuple, e.g. isinstance(self.expr, (Feature, Constant, DailyFeature)).
insertion_points.risk: This is the single most load-bearing one-line change and the easiest to forget. If skipped, the new node is treated as 'computed': assign_modes immediately does `spec = n.spec; if spec.face==...` on a leaf whose .spec is None (the Expression base-class default) -> AttributeError on first use, a loud but possibly confusing failure far from the actual root cause.

insertion_points.change: Add an isinstance(expr, DailyFeature) branch BEFORE the generic fallback: read a (C,D) or (S,C) slice from the new CubeView accessor, .unsqueeze(-1) to the (.,.,1) collapsed-cube shape apply_cube already expects (same trick _panel_slice uses at line 237), and call self._mask_cube(t, tradable) on it exactly like the Feature branch does.
insertion_points.risk: If the isinstance branch is added but the _mask_cube call is forgotten, a suspended stock-day's raw daily value would NOT be forced to NaN before feeding a cross_*/nt_* consumer, silently reintroducing the exact 'fake finite value' bug the engine's whole masking design exists to prevent (see test_mask_every_node). If the branch is omitted entirely, the new leaf falls through to `expr.field` + view.read_s/read_d and raises KeyError from CubeStore.field()'s 'store has no field' check — loud, not silent.

insertion_points.change: Add a branch that loads the new leaf's whole-view (D,S)-or-(S,D) array directly (P-rounds are never chunked, so load once, transpose/tensorize, no lo:hi slicing needed), mirroring the existing panels[c.key] branch at lines 361-362, and mask it the same way.
insertion_points.risk: HIGHEST-PROBABILITY first failure: _p_eligible will route almost every realistic use of a degenerate daily leaf (e.g. div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap)) straight into a P-mode round, which today has no fallback for any non-Constant leaf and raises RuntimeError('panel operand ... unavailable'). A design that only patches _load_leaf_cube (the S/D-mode path) and not this method will work for some trees and mysteriously crash on others depending purely on what else is in the expression. A SECOND, subtler risk if this branch is added without masking: an nd/cs operator (e.g. cs_rank, which DOES mix across all stocks on a day) would see an unmasked suspended-day value and could let it skew the ranks/reductions of OTHER stocks on that same day, even though that stock's own output cell later gets masked away — a cross-sectional leak, not merely a self-contained one.

insertion_points.change: Optionally add a branch for a bare new-leaf-as-root (factor := FloatCap with no wrapping operator).
insertion_points.risk: Low priority — the task's own examples only use the new leaf as an operand. Skipping it leaves a bare-root use raising ValueError (whose current text, 'is not a daily value', already names the gap) rather than misbehaving silently, so it is safe to defer to a second pass.

insertion_points.change: Implement _make_key() with a NEW key prefix (e.g. 'DF:{field}', distinct from Feature's 'F:{field}') and _infer_shape() returning either COLLAPSED or WIDE_DEGENERATE.
insertion_points.risk: The Shape choice is not cosmetic: it directly decides whether _p_eligible routes a consumer into P-mode, and whether in_expand(FloatCap,...) is grammar-legal under strict=True via operand_ok's `spec.restores_m -> sh.collapsed` check. No existing leaf type is 'always degenerate, always literally width-1, never genuinely full-width' in quite the way a daily leaf is, so there is no copy-paste precedent to lean on here (flagged in open_questions).

insertion_points.where: src/alphacube/store.py, new methods on CubeView (after tradable_d, ~line 447) backed by a new accessor on CubeStore/SegmentedCubeStore (near field()/read_cube(), lines 115-177 and 353-377)
insertion_points.change: Mirror the existing tradable()/tradable_s()/tradable_d() pattern exactly: compute+cache the whole-view (S,D) array once, reuse the existing private _rows helper and self.d0 offsetting for lo:hi slicing — but back it with a small in-memory numpy array per daily field (tens of MB at production scale) rather than an mmap.

result.summary: Read src/alphacube/engine/{dag,engine,schedule,kernels}.py and store.py's CubeView end-to-end. Compilation pipeline: Dag dedups expressions purely by structural expr.key() (no view identity anywhere in it) into a children-before-parents topo order; schedule.assign_modes gives every non-leaf node a mode (P/S/D) via a 3-pass bottom-up/top-down propagation keyed off each operator's declared face+compute_axis (axes.py's table), then plan_rounds greedily batches same-mode ready nodes into Rounds and marks cross-round edges as either an in-memory (S,D) 'panel' hand-off (degenerate values) or an on-disk (S,D,M)/(D,S,M) memmap 'boundary' (full-width values). CubeEngine.evaluate() runs P-rounds once on whole tensors and S/D-rounds chunk-by-chunk (chunk size from chunk_symbols/chunk_days or a chunk_bytes/M-scaled byte budget), stitching collapsed results into disjoint slices of a persistent (S,D) array and boundary results into a lazily-created memmap, both purely sequential (no merge step needed). Leaf-type dispatch is extremely concentrated: exactly 4 call sites across 2 files (dag.py's is_leaf isinstance tuple; engine.py's _load_leaf_cube, _leaf_panel, and _run_panel_round.operand) decide how a leaf becomes a tensor, and kernels.py never inspects leaf type at all — so adding a new 'daily leaf' needs zero kernels.py changes but DOES need all 3 engine.py sites updated (the P-mode operand loader is the one most likely to be missed, since _p_eligible will route most realistic uses of a degenerate daily leaf straight into P-mode) plus careful masking at each (verified by tracing the code: panels already carry an invariant that every resident value is pre-masked on suspended stock-days, which a new leaf's read-path must independently uphold or risk a cross-sectional leak through nd/cs operators). Warm-up for cross_*/ts_* rolling is entirely a caller convention (research.warmed_view pads the view's d0 backward and returns a trim count; the engine itself has no warm-up concept — it just evaluates the NaN-padded early rows like any other day). UniverseEngine is a pure post-hoc NaN-mask decorator on EvalResult.panels and needs no changes. Device is a uniform .to(device,dtype) everywhere with no device-conditional code; 'silent OOM' is not a dedicated mechanism in the 5 assigned files at all — it is the generic tolerant=True except-Exception in _run_cube_chunk/_run_panel_round, with the actual GPU memory cap set externally in cli.py and relied upon explicitly by mining/gp.py and mining/env.py. Tests build real on-disk synthetic stores (synthetic.py -> store.build_cube_store) via session-scoped fixtures and pin correctness/chunk-invariance against manually-computed per-symbol/per-day references, plus a sweep over every registered operator. CubeStore's on-disk format structurally assumes one shared (S,D,M) shape per store and has mmap/madvise/D-major-mirror machinery that exists only because minute cubes are gigabytes — a (S,D) daily field is tiny by comparison (~40MB/field at production scale), so CubeView's existing tradable()-style whole-view-cached-then-sliced pattern (not the mmap machinery) is the right template to copy. Design-level choices (where daily-field data physically lives, what Shape a daily leaf declares, whether it can be a bare root) are left as open questions rather than guessed.

facts.topic: Q1 class hierarchy
facts.detail: Expression (ABC, __slots__=('_key','_shape')) has exactly 4 concrete subclasses used by the grammar: Feature(field:str), Constant(value:float), _OpNode (abstract, holds spec/operands/window) with its 4 leaf subclasses Unary/Binary/Rolling/PairRolling (category-specific arity checks only), and GeneralCall (arbitrary arity, literal args, tuple-of-tensor args, 'exempt' operand positions). GeneralCall is never produced by make_node/the search grammar -- only the parser builds it, for research/legacy expressions reaching outside the 4-category grammar.

facts.topic: Q1 shape system
facts.detail: Shape is a frozen dataclass with exactly 2 independent booleans (collapsed, degenerate) plus an optional int width; 'daily' is NOT a third independent axis -- it is a read-only property that returns `self.degenerate` verbatim. 3 named module constants cover the combinations actually used: FULL=(False,False,None) = genuine per-minute tensor; COLLAPSED=(True,True,1) = day_*/restores_m-target, one real minute column; WIDE_DEGENERATE=(False,True,None) = full minute width but every column identical (Constant, in_expand's own output). A 4th, unnamed combination (arbitrary literal width 1<w<full, degenerate True or False) is produced ad hoc by _passthrough/GeneralCall for literal-width slices (e.g. in_slice(x,10,229) -> width=220). collapsed=True with degenerate=False is never constructed anywhere in the current code -- an invariant that holds by convention, not by an assertion.
facts.refs: expression.py:28-41 (Shape, FULL, COLLAPSED, WIDE_DEGENERATE), 34-36 (`daily` aliases `degenerate`), 175-196 (_passthrough/_output_shape produce the ad hoc 4th combination), test_expression.py:8-21 (test_shape_typing exercises all 3 named shapes plus FULL on a bare Feature)

facts.topic: Q1 make_node shape checks
facts.detail: make_node dispatches by spec.category to Unary/Binary/Rolling/PairRolling; _OpNode.__init__ is the single place that (a) checks operand count against the category's expected arity, (b) checks window presence against spec.requires_window, (c) calls operand_ok(spec, operand, strict) on every operand and raises ShapeError(_why_not(...)) on the first failure. GeneralCall.__init__ duplicates a SEPARATE, non-identical check (arity is unchecked/-1, tuple args unpacked, 'exempt' positions skipped) -- any change meant to also affect research/legacy (GeneralCall) trees must be made in both places.

facts.topic: Q1 is_valid_root
facts.detail: is_valid_root(expr) is exactly 3 conditions ANDed: (1) expr.shape.degenerate (both COLLAPSED and WIDE_DEGENERATE roots qualify); (2) the ROOT node's OWN spec.non_root must be False (non_root = boolean_output or coarse_output, axes.py:112-114) -- this is a root-only check, it does NOT walk descendants, so a boolean op anywhere BELOW the root (e.g. pow_05(eq(a,b))) is NOT caught by is_valid_root at all; (3) `any(isinstance(n, Feature) for n in expr.nodes())` -- at least one Feature leaf anywhere in the tree (constant-only trees like sigmoid(5) are rejected).
facts.refs: expression.py:398-404; test_expression.py:8-25 (table incl. is_gt0(day_mean(Ret))->root=False, cs_rank(mul(day_mean(Close),2))->root=True), test_expression.py:43-45 (constant-only tree)

facts.topic: Q1 the real defense against 'laundered' booleans
facts.detail: Because is_valid_root only inspects the ROOT's own flag, the actual mechanism keeping boolean/trivial operators out of search trees ENTIRELY (not just as roots) is Registry.searchable(include_boolean=False), which filters them out of the operator VOCABULARY a generator may place anywhere in a tree. catalog.py's own docstring records a real incident: pow_05(eq(a,b)) reached rank 1 of a generation with spurious |IC| 0.58 before this filter existed. So 'declare an operator real-valued' (Q4) and is_valid_root (Q1) are two independent levers; fixing the OpSpec flag at registration time (as Partura's dataclasses.replace already does) automatically satisfies BOTH -- re-admits the op to searchable() AND lets it be a legal root -- with one change.

facts.topic: Q1 key() construction
facts.detail: key() is lazily computed once and cached on the instance via object.__setattr__ (bypassing __slots__ immutability) into the base class's _key slot. Per-kind, type-tagged format: Feature -> 'F:{field}'; Constant -> 'C:{value!r}' (exact float repr, so 1.0 vs 1.0000001 differ); _OpNode -> 'O:{spec.name}({child.key(),...}){|wN}'; GeneralCall -> 'G:{spec.name}({rendered args})' where a literal renders as 'L:{a!r}', a tuple-of-exprs as '[e.key(),...]'. key() (not object identity) is the sole structural-equality/hash basis (__eq__/__hash__ both delegate to it) and is consumed well beyond expression.py: GP population dedup and ban-list lookups (mining/gp.py), the mutation/growth env (mining/env.py), seed/boosting dedup (mining/boosting.py, pipeline.py), and DAG common-subexpression identity (engine/dag.py).
facts.refs: expression.py:65-74 (key()/_make_key base), 116-117 (Feature), 132-133 (Constant), 226-229 (_OpNode), 335-342 (GeneralCall); test_expression.py:48-55; consumers: mining/gp.py:260,374,444,463,535,558,591,716-717,883; mining/env.py:144,204,239,275; mining/boosting.py:100-102; mining/generator.py:65,145,148; engine/dag.py:17,61; pipeline.py:107-108

facts.topic: Q2 leaf kinds and field-name source
facts.detail: Today there are exactly 2 leaf kinds: Feature(field) and Constant(value). CUBE_FIELDS=('Open','High','Low','Close','Volume','Vwap','Ret','Amt') (catalog.py:375) is the sole canonical field-name source, passed into Registry(fields) by build_registry(); parser.name() checks `ident in self.reg.fields` first (case-sensitive canonical name), then FIELD_ALIASES (lowercase/short spellings: close,open,high,low,vol,volume,vwap,ret,amt,returns -> one of the 8 canonical names), then DAILY_MACROS, then DAILY_NAME_ALIASES -- in that precedence order.
facts.refs: catalog.py:375 (CUBE_FIELDS), catalog.py:324-326,405-406 (Registry.fields wiring), parser.py:39-42 (FIELD_ALIASES), parser.py:133-143 (name() dispatch order)

facts.topic: Q2 constant recognition
facts.detail: A bare numeric literal becomes Constant iff `isinstance(node.value,(int,float)) and not isinstance(node.value,bool)` -- the explicit bool exclusion matters because Python's ast.Constant.value for True/False IS an int instance (bool subclasses int); without the guard, True/False would silently become Constant(1.0)/Constant(0.0). The same not-isinstance(x,bool) guard is repeated at every literal boundary: unary-minus constant folding, GeneralCall literal args, window_literal, and GeneralCall.literal_width.
facts.refs: parser.py:112 (convert), 189 and 193-195 (call(), GeneralCall literal args + negative-literal), 220-223 (window_literal); expression.py:330-332 (literal_width)

facts.topic: Q2 strict vs lenient operand rules
facts.detail: operand_ok(spec, operand, strict) has 2 strict-gated relaxations, both OFF by default (strict=True is the search grammar's rule): (a) restores_m (in_expand): strict requires operand.shape.collapsed exactly (width==1 AND degenerate); non-strict only requires operand.shape.degenerate (so a WIDE_DEGENERATE operand, e.g. mul(day_mean(Close),2), is accepted in in_expand only when non-strict). (b) needs_full_m (which covers BOTH in_*/day_* (face=='dt' and family in ('in','day')) AND nt_*): if the operand genuinely varies per minute (not degenerate) it is always fine; if degenerate, strict always rejects, non-strict accepts ONLY when the operator itself reduces_m (day_*) AND the operand is specifically collapsed (width==1) -- i.e. the non-strict carve-out exists for day_*-over-day_*, never for in_*/nt_* over a degenerate operand. needs_daily (nd face: cs_*/ts_*) has no strict/non-strict distinction at all: it only ever requires sh.degenerate. cross_* and elementwise ops are unrestricted in both modes (fall through to the final `return True`).
facts.refs: expression.py:144-172 (operand_ok, _why_not); axes.py:88-96 (needs_full_m, needs_daily); test_expression.py:28-40 (test_shape_errors, all under strict); test_general_call.py:47-49 (parse(...,strict=True) rejects, parse_legacy allows the day_*-over-width-1 case)

facts.topic: Q2 coerce_daily and allow_general
facts.detail: allow_general=False makes self.full=None, so any name outside the 4-category registry raises ParseError('unknown operator') instead of falling into GeneralCall -- the switch between 'search-grammar-only' and the 'research/legacy full surface'. coerce_daily=True sets self.daily_fields=True for the WHOLE parse iff the expression tree contains NO minute-level operator at all (checked once up front by uses_minute_operators, which looks only at face in ('dt','nt') after alias/arity resolution); when true, every bare field name resolves to its DAILY macro (Feature('Close') becomes day_last(Close) etc, via DAILY_OF_FIELD) instead of the raw minute Feature. If the tree DOES use a minute operator, bare fields stay minute-level, and coercion instead happens node-locally in .coerce()/.daily_of(): only when a raw-field subtree is fed directly as an operand of an ND-face (cs_*/ts_*) operator is it wrapped in its day_* macro; coercion recurses through 'shared'-face (elementwise) ancestors but raises ParseError if it hits a genuine minute-level (dt/nt) subtree it cannot coerce.
facts.refs: parser.py:74-108 (_Parser.__init__, parse(), uses_minute_operators), 227-264 (apply/coerce/daily_of), 284-293 (parse/parse_legacy entry points); test_general_call.py:69-77 (test_daily_coercion_for_nd_operators)

facts.topic: Q3 which operator families can consume a (D,S)-no-minute-axis leaf unchanged
facts.detail: If the new leaf's _infer_shape() returns exactly COLLAPSED (collapsed=True, degenerate=True, width=1 -- reusing the SAME Shape already used for a day_* output, not a new 4th kind), then operand_ok admits it with ZERO code changes for: cs_*/ts_* (nd face, needs_daily branch only checks sh.degenerate); cross_* (dt/cross family is NOT in the ('in','day') tuple that defines needs_full_m, so cross_* operators impose no shape restriction at all -- confirmed by test_shape_typing's cross_mean(day_mean(Close),5)->COLLAPSED,root=True); every elementwise/'shared' op (final fallback `return True`); and in_expand specifically (restores_m: sh.collapsed is satisfied even under strict). day_*/in_* (dt, family in ('in','day')) and nt_* (face=='nt') REJECT it under strict (needs_full_m requires genuine per-minute variation); under non-strict/legacy they reject it too for in_*/nt_* but would ACCEPT it for day_* specifically (the existing 'day_* over width-1' carve-out, originally meant for literal in_slice(...,w=1) subtrees) -- whether that carve-out should also silently accept the new leaf is a real design choice, not something the current code decides for a genuinely new leaf type.
facts.refs: expression.py:144-162 (operand_ok), axes.py:88-92,117-126 (needs_full_m / compute_axis_for -- cross excluded from the ('in','day') tuple), expression.py:186-196 (_output_shape), test_expression.py:8-21 (cross_mean(day_mean(Close),5) case)

facts.topic: Q3 current elementwise rule between a full-minute tensor and a day_*/degenerate one (static type level)
facts.detail: operand_ok imposes NO shape restriction on 'shared'-face (elementwise: add/sub/mul/div/eq/...) operators at all -- the final catch-all `return True` applies regardless of either operand's shape. So add(day_mean(Close), Close) IS a legal expression TODAY under the static type rules, with shape computed by _passthrough: given one COLLAPSED and one FULL operand, result.collapsed=False, result.degenerate=False, i.e. the combined shape collapses to FULL-equivalent. This is directly confirmed by the existing test suite, which already relies on day_*-vs-raw-minute-Feature mixing being legal: sub(Close, in_expand(day_mean(Close), 241)) parses to shape FULL (not a root).
facts.refs: expression.py:144-162 (operand_ok final `return True`), 175-183 (_passthrough), test_expression.py:14 (`sub(Close, in_expand(day_mean(Close), 241))` -> FULL)

facts.topic: Q3 same rule at the RUNTIME/engine level (outside the 3 assigned files, read for grounding)
facts.detail: At execution time the legality above is realised two different ways depending on operator family: for non-elementwise M-axis/D-axis ops (in_*, day_*, cross_*), engine/kernels.py's _align_widths() EXPLICITLY broadcasts any width-1 (day-collapsed/constant) operand up to the common minute width via `.expand(...).contiguous()` before the kernel runs (two genuinely different widths both >1 raises a ValueError there). For a node whose OWN family=='elementwise', apply_cube() skips _align_widths/_pre_collapse entirely (kernels.py:193-194) and calls the raw torch op directly -- it relies purely on PyTorch's native trailing-dimension broadcasting of the materialized (A,B,1) tensor against (A,B,M). A COLLAPSED node is kept with a literal trailing axis of size 1 inside a round (never squeezed to bare (A,B)); only at a ROUND BOUNDARY (schedule.py) does ANY degenerate node -- COLLAPSED or WIDE_DEGENERATE alike, the check is purely `n.shape.degenerate`, not `.collapsed` -- get handed off as a bare 2-D (S,D) panel (schedule.py:142-150). Consequence for the new leaf: if its raw stored form is read in as bare (A,B) (no trailing axis at all), it will NOT broadcast correctly against an (A,B,M) cube tensor under native torch rules (trailing dims would compare B against M); it must be materialised as (A,B,1) wherever it enters a cube-mode round, exactly mirroring how a day_* output already behaves -- this reshape point lives in whatever code reads leaves into a chunk, which is in engine.py/store.py, outside the 3 files I was assigned and NOT verified by me (see open_questions).
facts.refs: engine/kernels.py:73-77 (_expand_like), 122-143 (_align_widths), 186-229 (apply_cube, elementwise short-circuit at 193-194), 232-240 (apply_panel); engine/schedule.py:57-64 (_p_eligible), 138-150 (panel-hand-off keyed on `.shape.degenerate` only)

facts.topic: Q3 daily.py is NOT the mechanism needed
facts.detail: alphacube/daily.py's DailyData/daily_from_view/DAILY_FIELD_EXPRESSIONS are downstream CONSUMERS of the engine (they call CubeEngine.evaluate() on day_* macros of the minute cube and wrap the resulting (D,S) numpy arrays for pools/models/portfolio/backtest) -- they do not touch Expression, Shape, make_node, or the parser, and cannot represent a field with NO minute-cube definition at all (FloatCap has no day_*(minute_field) reduction to call). A true 'daily leaf' for 甲 needs a new Expression leaf class, not an extension of daily.py.

facts.topic: Q4 OpSpec fields
facts.detail: OpSpec (frozen dataclass) stores: name, face, family, category, arity, requires_window, fn, kernel_id, compute_axis, reduces_m, restores_m, lookahead, boolean_output, trivial_boolean, resource_risk, coarse_output, windows. Derived properties (not stored): needs_full_m, needs_daily, allowed_modes, non_root(=boolean_output or coarse_output).

facts.topic: Q4 _validate's own smoke test (accept/skip, NOT the boolean probe)
facts.detail: _validate(name, meta) decides only whether an operator is ACCEPTED into the registry at all (else recorded as a SkipRecord with a reason) by confirming its real output shape matches its declared category. For in_expand (RESTORES_M_NAMES): calls fn(x,3) on x=_sample(rows=7,cols=1,seed=1) (uniform [0.5,1.5), via torch.rand()+0.5) and requires output shape exactly (7,3). For everything else: classify(meta) maps (arity, requires_window, pair) to one of unary/binary/rolling/pair_rolling (returns None, i.e. reject, if no combination matches); _smoke_call feeds _sample(seed=1) (rows=7,cols=5) and, for binary/pair_rolling, a second _sample(seed=2); a 'day'-family kernel must collapse its last dim to size 1, every other kernel's output shape must equal its input's shape exactly, else rejected.

facts.topic: Q4 the 3 empirical cardinality/cost probes feeding OpSpec flags
facts.detail: boolean_output/coarse_output come from _probe_distinct_values: torch.Generator().manual_seed(7), x=randn(40,9) then y=randn(40,9) drawn SEQUENTIALLY off the same generator (not independently reseeded); if restores_m, x is sliced to its first column; dispatch by grammar category (unary/binary/rolling/else=pair_rolling) calls the kernel once and counts DISTINCT FINITE values after flattening -- boolean_output=(distinct<=2), coarse_output=(2<distinct<=3). trivial_boolean = boolean_output AND _probe_constant_capable: manual_seed(11), base=rand(40,9)+0.5 (strictly positive [0.5,1.5)), other=another draw off the same generator, tried over 4 input families in order -- (base,other), (-base,-other), (base,base), (randn,randn) off the continuing generator -- returning True on the FIRST family where the finite output collapses to <=1 distinct value (or is entirely non-finite/empty after filtering). resource_risk = name in SEARCH_FORBIDDEN_KERNELS({nt_ts_pearson,nt_ts_spearman,in_multireg}) OR name in POSITIONALLY_UNSAFE_KERNELS({pow}) OR (face!='nd' AND _probe_per_element_python(...)); the 3rd disjunct short-circuits (the expensive line-counting probe never runs for a name already caught by the first two, nor for any nd-face kernel). _probe_per_element_python (manual_seed(5), rand()+0.5) counts Python bytecode LINE events (via sys.settrace, deterministic/machine-independent) executed inside alphacube.operators at shapes (16,48) vs (64,48) vs (16,192); flags resource_risk if either larger run executes more than 2x+20 the baseline's lines (a vectorised kernel runs the same line count regardless of size; a Python-looping one scales).

facts.topic: Q4 lookahead is NOT probed -- it is a hardcoded constant, verified by a separate test
facts.detail: Unlike boolean/trivial/resource_risk, `lookahead` is set purely from static frozenset membership: `lookahead=(kernel_id.split('.')[-1] in LOOKAHEAD_KERNELS)` where LOOKAHEAD_KERNELS={'ts_shift','cross_shift','in_local_mean'} is a manually curated constant -- build_registry performs NO random-input probe for lookahead. It is instead cross-checked at TEST time (not build time) by a dedicated perturbation test that mutates data strictly after t=20 and checks whether early outputs change.

facts.topic: Q4 a separate, differently-scoped constant with a similar name
facts.detail: RESOURCE_RISK_KERNELS = frozenset({'ts_pearson','nt_ts_pearson','nt_ts_spearman','in_multireg'}) (catalog.py:56) is NOT the same thing as the OpSpec.resource_risk FIELD computed by _make_spec: it is a hand-picked, separately-exported constant (re-exported as DEFERRED_RESOURCE_OPERATORS by calculate.py) used by calculate.py / mining/gp.py / scripts/eval_legacy_factors.py to decide what to defer computationally for MEMORY reasons; it deliberately INCLUDES ts_pearson (the ND-face kernel), which the registry's own OpSpec.resource_risk correctly keeps OUT of SEARCH_FORBIDDEN_KERNELS (ts_pearson is ND-face, O(1942x cheaper) than its NT twin) -- this split is intentional and documented in catalog.py's own module docstring, not a bug, but the near-identical naming is a real foot-gun worth knowing before touching either.
facts.refs: catalog.py:44-56 (module docstring explaining the ND-vs-NT cost asymmetry + RESOURCE_RISK_KERNELS), calculate.py:33, mining/gp.py:38,267, test_mining.py:166-170 (asserts SEARCH_FORBIDDEN_KERNELS is a strict subset of RESOURCE_RISK_KERNELS and that calculate.py's alias is the SAME object)

facts.topic: Q4 why in_sustain_stddev is mis-flagged boolean_output -- verified by direct execution
facts.detail: in_sustain_stddev(mask, data, d, start_offset=0, num=False) (dt_in.py:832-843) is a pair_rolling op whose FIRST operand is semantically a {0,1} trigger mask (`torch.where(mask==1)` locates trigger cells); but every build-time probe (_probe_distinct_values's randn(40,9); all 4 of _probe_constant_capable's families, including (base,other) in [0.5,1.5)) feeds it CONTINUOUS random floats, which (for a continuous distribution) essentially never equal exactly 1.0. I re-ran both probes directly: on the exact probe input (manual_seed(7), randn(40,9) x2), `(x==1).sum()`==0, so `_get_rowwise_windows` finds zero trigger rows and the function returns an all-NaN (40,9) tensor every time (fill_value=NaN since num defaults False) -> 0 distinct finite values (<=2) -> boolean_output=True; the same all-NaN/empty-after-filter outcome on every one of _probe_constant_capable's 4 families -> trivial_boolean=True too. in_sustain_stddev is one of AlphaCube's OWN built-in kernels (not in Partura's ops_ext.py NEW_OPERATORS list), so Partura's current blanket flag-clearing (which only iterates NEW_OPERATORS) does NOT fix it -- it stays mis-flagged even with partura.ops_ext loaded.

facts.topic: Q4 how 'declare real-valued' is currently faked, and why it's safe to make it a first-class hook
facts.detail: Partura's ops_ext.install() (ops_ext.py:729-759) does NOT touch the probes; it runs the normal (misflagging) build, then post-hoc overwrites the OpSpec via `dataclasses.replace(sp, boolean_output=False, trivial_boolean=False)` for every name in NEW_OPERATORS (+nt twins) found flagged -- leaves coarse_output untouched, is keyed by an externally-maintained hardcoded name list, and is applied via monkeypatching the catalog.build_registry function object itself (guarded by a `build_registry._partura` sentinel so it only wraps once). A first-class alternative: add a boolean kwarg to operators/common.py's op() decorator (op(...), stored into the OPERATOR_REGISTRY[name] meta dict) that catalog.py's _make_spec reads and, when True, SKIPS calling _probe_distinct_values/_probe_constant_capable entirely (forcing boolean_output=trivial_boolean=coarse_output=False) instead of overriding their result. This is safe for the 'byte-identical when no new argument is passed' constraint for two independent reasons: (1) every existing @op(...) call site keeps the new kwarg at its default (False/off), so no existing OpSpec changes; (2) each probe already constructs its OWN fresh, locally-seeded torch.Generator() (manual_seed(7) / manual_seed(11) / manual_seed(5)) rather than touching any shared/global RNG stream, so skipping the probe call for a declared-real kernel cannot perturb any OTHER kernel's probe outcome or the random stream the search grammar itself draws from.
facts.refs: ops_ext.py:729-759 (install()); operators/common.py:56-71 (op() decorator + OPERATOR_REGISTRY dict shape); catalog.py:378-402 (_make_spec, where the new kwarg would short-circuit); catalog.py:88-90,196-197,280-281 (each probe's self-contained torch.Generator())

result.summary: Read-only fact map for AlphaCube's expression/parser/catalog type system (files: src/alphacube/expression.py, parser.py, catalog.py, axes.py, operators/common.py, plus fullcatalog.py, daily.py, tradability.py, engine/kernels.py, engine/schedule.py, scripts/tearsheet.py, synthetic.py and the relevant tests/*.py, all read for grounding -- only expression.py/parser.py/catalog.py/operators-common were the assigned targets). No files were modified; one throwaway introspection script was written to /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/design/probe_boolean_flags.py and run read-only via PYTHONPATH=/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src ~/.venvs/alphacube/bin/python to empirically verify (not guess) which operators the catalog's boolean/trivial-boolean probes mis-flag.\n\nHeadline findings: (1) Expression's type system is 2 leaf kinds (Feature/Constant) + 4 operator-node kinds (Unary/Binary/Rolling/PairRolling, all built through the single make_node/_OpNode.__init__ check) + GeneralCall (a second, separate check, used only by the parser for research/legacy expressions). Shape is just 2 booleans (collapsed, degenerate) + optional width -- 'daily' is a property ALIAS of degenerate, not an independent axis; 3 named constants (FULL/COLLAPSED/WIDE_DEGENERATE) cover what's actually built. (2) is_valid_root is a narrow 3-condition root-only check; the real defense against a 'boolean laundered through arithmetic' root is Registry.searchable()'s vocabulary filter, a different mechanism entirely -- important for designing the 'declare real-valued' hook, since fixing the OpSpec flag at registration time satisfies both mechanisms at once. (3) A new (D,S)-no-minute-axis daily leaf, if given shape=COLLAPSED (reusing exactly the Shape a day_* output already uses), is accepted with ZERO code changes by cs_*/ts_*, cross_*, all elementwise ops, and in_expand; it is rejected by day_*/in_*/nt_* under strict (and by in_*/nt_* under legacy too) -- all verified from the actual operand_ok/axes.py logic, cross-checked against engine/kernels.py+schedule.py to confirm how a day_*-vs-raw-Feature elementwise mix is materialised today (COLLAPSED kept as a real (A,B,1) trailing axis in-round; only degenerate-ness, not collapsed-ness, decides the (S,D)-bare-panel round-boundary hand-off). (4) I ran catalog.py's ORIGINAL (unpatched) build_registry against Partura's 45 new operators and confirmed empirically -- not assumed -- that exactly 9 base names (day_flat_ratio, day_zero_ratio, day_flat_run_max, day_at_max_ratio, day_at_min_ratio, day_distinct_ratio, cross_flat_ratio, cs_bucket_demean, cs_bucket_zscore) get boolean_output=trivial_boolean=True from 2 distinct causes (exact-equality tests that never fire on continuous random floats; a decile-bucket `n>=2` validity gate that never fires with only 9 probe columns), and separately confirmed exactly why AlphaCube's own in_sustain_stddev is mis-flagged (its mask operand never equals 1.0 under continuous random probe data, so it always returns all-NaN). (5) None of the existing tests pin down an exact boolean/trivial-flagged operator set, so today's mis-flags are silent -- a new test asserting the full set (or at least the known-good/known-bad lists) would catch regressions.

facts.topic: 1. mutate_window/mutate_constant bypass acceptable -- CONFIRMED with a repro, not just code-reading
facts.detail: mutate_window (generator.py:221-234) and mutate_constant (generator.py:236-246) both end with `return child if is_valid_root(child) else None` -- they never call self.acceptable(child), so the banned_substructures check is skipped. A read-only repro (sweeping TypedTreeGenerator(default_registry(), n_minutes=24, max_depth=4) populations over many seeds) found concrete counterexamples in the FIRST seed tried, e.g. tree `ts_corr(ts_spearman(day_argmin(Low), 10), cross_quantile_q75(day_hurst(Volume), 30), 40)` with `O:day_hurst(F:Volume)` banned: mutate_window changed the UNRELATED node's window (ts_spearman 10->30), returned a child that still contains `day_hurst(Volume)` untouched, and gen.acceptable(child) is False on that same child -- i.e. a tree acceptable() would reject is returned anyway. Same pattern reproduced for mutate_constant (e.g. victim `O:day_skew(F:High)`, mutating an unrelated `add(-2, ...)` constant). tests/test_mining.py:364-386 (test_banned_substructures_cannot_enter_by_any_route) already loops mutate_window/mutate_constant over ONE (seed=4, victim) pair and currently passes -- it does not reliably exercise this gap because whether it triggers depends on whether the randomly-chosen carrier tree happens to have a mutable window/constant node unrelated to the banned node.

facts.topic: 1. RNG consumption order / backward-compat hazard for a weighted _pick hook
facts.detail: Every self._rng call in generator.py matters for bit-identical replay: generate() consumes .randint then .random (full/daily split) then whatever _gen/_build/_pick/_window_for/_leaf consume recursively. _pick currently calls self._rng.choice(...) (via _randbelow, typically 1 word of the MT19937 state per draw). Empirically verified (small script): random.Random(12345).choice(['x','y','z']) advances the internal state index by 1 word, while .choices(['x','y','z'], weights=[1,1,1])[0] (uniform weights, still explicit) advances it by 2 words (one random() call) -- so a weighted-_pick hook that unconditionally switches to self._rng.choices(...) does NOT reproduce the old stream even when all weights are 1.0/absent. Partura's idea_search.py patched `pick()` always calls self._rng.choices(...) (never the original .choice), including in its 'control' arm where weights are uniform -- so despite the script's own docstring claiming the control arm is 'the same GP ... uniform sampling', it is not bit-for-bit identical to an unpatched AlphaCube run from the first _pick call onward.

facts.topic: 1. Leaf sampling (fields/constants/_collapse_leaf) and what daily-leaf support would touch
facts.detail: _leaf(req): req=='full' -> Feature(self._rng.choice(self.fields)) (one rng call); req=='daily' -> Constant(self._rng.choice(self.constants)) (one rng call, ALWAYS a Constant today -- there is no 'daily field' leaf type at all); req=='collapsed' raises ShapeError (no leaf satisfies it). _collapse_leaf(spec): builds a minimal daily tree by wrapping 1 or 2 raw-field Feature leaves in a day_*/reducing operator -- it is the ONLY way a per-minute Field becomes daily-shaped today. To make a new daily-frequency field (FloatCap etc.) sampleable as a leaf: (1) a new Expression leaf type parallel to Feature/Constant is needed whose .shape is already daily/degenerate (Feature is always minute-indexed); (2) TypedTreeGenerator needs a parallel self.daily_fields list threaded through __init__ next to fields/constants; (3) _leaf's req=='daily' branch is the exact insertion point, but today it unconditionally does exactly one self._rng.choice(self.constants) call -- adding a field-vs-constant coin flip there changes the RNG shape for every existing run unless gated behind 'no daily fields registered -> identical code path'; (4) tokens.py needs a parallel DailyFieldToken + grammar-mask entries; (5) the ban-key grammar (gp.py's _BAN_KEY regex, 'F:<field>'/'C:<value>' leaf prefixes) would need a third leaf prefix convention for ban keys that bottom out at a daily field.

facts.topic: 2. Seed filtering (_seeded_population / __init__ seed intake)
facts.detail: __init__ keeps only seeds that are: acceptable() (legal root, not banned), not contains_lookahead, not self._refused (not using a skip_kernels name), within seed_max_depth if set, every node's spec either None, a GeneralCall, or named in the search vocabulary (allowed = {sp.name for sp in self.generator.specs}), and not containing a GeneralCall whose '_legacy' kernel is in RESOURCE_RISK_KERNELS. _seeded_population(block): on first use, scores ALL seeds in batches of EXEMPLAR_BATCH=150 via self.fitness(..., cache=False) and sorts by that fitness (ties stable); then picks seed_keep (default population_size//2) seeds, re-checking generator.acceptable(e) and deduping by clustering.skeleton_key(e) (one per skeleton); writes checkpoint_dir/seeds_used.csv when a checkpoint_dir is set; fills the rest of the population with generator.generate_population(...).

facts.topic: 2. fitness/_score caching
facts.detail: _panels(population, cache=True) caches evaluated (D,S) panels in self._panel_cache (OrderedDict) keyed by expr.key(), LRU-evicted at BOTH an item cap (panel_cache_items) and a byte cap (panel_cache_bytes) via _evict_panels. _score(key, panel) caches fitness dict {ic, rank_ic, turnover, fit, ...} in self._scores keyed by expr.key() -- a panel is a pure function of its structural key. fitness(population) calls _panels then, if self._rich (fitness_kind!='ic' or turnover_penalty>0), calls self._score(...)['fit'] per live tree under self._scorer (a PanelScorer/LongScorer/LongHitScorer instance); otherwise uses the plain-IC path via metrics.batched_ic across all live panels at once with inline coverage/min_scored_days gating. A SEPARATE rank-ban pass follows (if self._rank_ban set), demoting any panel matching a banned family to -inf and caching the per-generation verdict in self._rank_verdict keyed by (expr key, self._rank_ban.version).

facts.topic: 2. mine() generation loop and the wall-clock-budget insertion point
facts.detail: mine(budget, on_generation=None): n_gen = ceil(budget/population_size); seeds the first population via _seeded_population(1); then `for g in range(n_gen): population = self._next_generation(...); raw = self.fitness(population); fit = self._archive_update(...); ...; if checkpoint_every and (g+1)%checkpoint_every==0: write_checkpoint(...); if rolling_block and (g+1)%rolling_block==0 and g+1<n_gen: self._roll(...) + regenerate population`. The natural place to add a wall-clock budget is inside this `for g in range(n_gen):` loop (a `break` after the per-generation bookkeeping, before/alongside the checkpoint/rolling-block checks) -- the loop already has t0=time.perf_counter() at the top of mine(). Risk: an early break must still reach self._commit() (the single call that offers the archive to the pool) at the end of mine(), and if a roll just happened the final `if self.rolling_block and ... len(self._archive) > len(self._block_seen): self._roll(...)` (the 'final unrolled block still gets scored' call) must also still run so the last block's on_block callback fires.
facts.refs: src/alphacube/mining/gp.py:733-747 (loop header), 747-794 (body incl. rolling-block and final roll), 785 (_commit)

facts.topic: 2. checkpoint CSV columns (scorer.columns contract)
facts.detail: write_checkpoint writes columns: rank,fitness,<score_ic,score_rank_ic,score_turnover + score_<name> for every name in self._scorer.columns>,dups,ic_mean,icir,rank_ic,coverage,n_days,annualized_return,sharpe,max_drawdown,turnover,sharpe_net,expression. `parts = ('ic','rank_ic','turnover') + tuple(getattr(self._scorer,'columns',()))` is how a scorer declares extra diagnostic fields -- PanelScorer has no .columns (so parts is just the base 3); LongScorer.columns=LONG_COLUMNS (9 fields); LongHitScorer overrides self.columns dynamically in __init__ from its active weights. facts.topic: 3. Three scorer constructors
facts.detail: PanelScorer(target, *, kind='rank_ic', turnover_penalty=0.14, signed=False, top_frac=BOOK_TOP_FRAC, min_coverage=0.5, min_scored_days=0.5) -- raises ValueError if kind not in ('ic','rank_ic'). LongScorer(target, *, cost_per_side=0.0015, top_frac=BOOK_TOP_FRAC, side_frac=LONG_SIDE_FRAC, min_coverage=0.5, min_scored_days=0.5, min_distinct=LONG_MIN_DISTINCT, max_boundary_ties=LONG_MAX_BOUNDARY_TIES, max_code_order=LONG_MAX_CODE_ORDER, weights=None, scales=None, unit=LONG_UNIT). NONE of the three accepts a generic **kwargs catch-all except LongHitScorer's own explicit **kw (which it forwards to LongScorer.__init__, which has none) -- so any new kwarg (e.g. a future `dates=`) passed uniformly by a registry-based make_scorer would TypeError on PanelScorer and LongScorer today.

facts.topic: 4. argparse choices= would reject a plugin-registered --fitness value regardless of where --plugin is loaded inside cmd_mine
facts.detail: cli.py's main() is `args = build_parser().parse_args(argv); return args.fn(args)` -- parse_args() validates --fitness against its static `choices=('ic','rank_ic','long','long_hit')` (and --miner against MINERS) BEFORE args.fn(args) (i.e. cmd_mine) is ever called. Loading a --plugin module inside cmd_mine (per the previous fact) is therefore always too late to let argparse accept a plugin-registered fitness-kind value on the command line -- parse_args() would already have raised SystemExit(2). Either --fitness's static choices= must be dropped (validate membership in the live scorer registry after the plugin loads, inside cmd_mine/run_mining) or the plugin module must be imported in a pre-parse scan of sys.argv before build_parser().parse_args() runs.

facts.topic: 5. Vocabulary token order
facts.detail: Vocabulary.__init__ builds tokens in this fixed order: [BEG, SEP] + [FeatureToken(f) for f in self.fields] (registry.fields order unless overridden) + [OperatorToken(s.name) for s in self.operators] (self.operators = sorted(specs, key=lambda s: s.name) -- ALPHABETICAL) + [ConstantToken(c) for c in self.constants] + [WindowToken(w) for w in self.windows] (sorted ascending union of every operator's windows plus n_minutes, unless windows is passed explicitly). Indices are assigned by this concatenation order, so any plugin-added operator shifts every index after the operator block alphabetically by name -- this is itself a stable property as long as the vocabulary is rebuilt fresh each run (nothing persists indices across runs).

facts.topic: 5. action_mask / grammar
facts.detail: TokenEnv.action_mask() (env.py:72-77) just calls self._builder.valid_next_tokens() and sets those indices True; the real logic is ExpressionBuilder.valid_next_tokens() (tokens.py:211-238): Feature and Constant tokens are ALWAYS offered (no restriction); Window tokens only if stack top is an Expression; each operator is offered only if its arity/window/operand-count preconditions hold AND expression.operand_ok(spec, operand) passes for every operand (the DT/ND/NT type-compatibility rule); SEP is offered only when the stack holds exactly one Expression that is_valid_root.

facts.topic: 5. BatchRewarder reward computation order and ban checks
facts.detail: BatchRewarder.rewards(exprs) order, per candidate: (1) structural-ban check BEFORE evaluation -- `if banned_substructures and (one_layer_keys(e) & banned_substructures): penalty` (cheap, no engine call); (2) batch-evaluate panels via self.panels(...); (3) score via self.scorer.score(p64) if a scorer is set (cached per expr key in self._solo_scores), else fall back to the plain Pearson-IC path; reject (penalty) if the solo fitness/IC is not finite; (4) THEN the rank-similarity ban -- `if rank_ban is not None and len(rank_ban) and rank_ban.match(p64) is not None: penalty` (after scoring, since it needs the evaluated panel); (5) min_solo gate (`_outside`, pays the solo fitness floored at half the penalty the FIRST time a sub-bar candidate is seen, penalty on repeats -- tracked in self._paid_outside); (6) optional novelty vs pool members; (7) pool.try_add; (8) reward = solo fitness (reward_kind=='solo'), or the pool's recombined fit (scorer set), or the raw pool IC.

facts.topic: 5. RL ban-key validation gap (confirmed: check_ban_key is never called on the RL path)
facts.detail: GPMiner.__init__ validates every banned_substructures key via check_ban_key(key, registry, generator.fields) (gp.py:139-155 defines it; gp.py:248-251 calls it) -- a malformed key raises ValueError at construction time. Grepping the whole repo shows check_ban_key is called from exactly 2 places: GPMiner.__init__ (gp.py:250) and the standalone offline lint script scripts/check_ban_keys.py (used in scripts/gp_chain.sh as a pre-flight check on a shell script's --ban arguments, not at run time). pipeline.py's RL branch builds `BatchRewarder(..., banned_substructures=tuple(cfg.get('banned_substructures', ())), ...)` (pipeline.py:407-410) and BatchRewarder.__init__ just does `self.banned_substructures = frozenset(banned_substructures)` (env.py:131) with ZERO validation -- a malformed --ban key on an RL run silently never matches anything instead of raising at startup like the GP path does.

facts.topic: 5. RL token-bias precedent (narrow, SEP-only today)
facts.detail: AlphaGenMiner/AlphaForgeMiner/AlphaQCMMiner/AlphaSAGEMiner each have an identical pattern in their actor network's __init__: `sep_index: Optional[int]=None, sep_bias: float=4.0` and, if sep_index is given, `self.<final_layer>.bias[sep_index] = sep_bias` -- a cold-start trick to make episodes terminate often enough to bootstrap the sparse pool reward. This is the ONLY existing 'token bias' mechanism, it is hardcoded to the SEP token specifically, and there is no general 'bias operator token X by weight W' mechanism analogous to GP's _pick weighting on any RL miner. PPOWarmStartQCMMiner (warmstart.py) was not in this set in a direct grep for sep_bias (it likely reuses AlphaQCMMiner's network; not independently confirmed).

facts.topic: idea_search.py patch mechanism -- generator hooks (global class monkeypatch, restored per arm)
facts.detail: `T = agen.TypedTreeGenerator; _acceptable, _pick = T.acceptable, T._pick`; `install(arm)` defines closures `pick`/`acceptable` and does `T._pick, T.acceptable = pick, acceptable` -- this mutates the CLASS (every instance process-wide), not a per-instance hook; it is restored with `T._pick, T.acceptable = _pick, _acceptable` immediately after each arm's run_mining() call (idea_search.py:274). `pick` always calls `self._rng.choices(...)` (weighted, even when every weight is 1.0 in the 'control' arm) and zeroes out weight for any AlphaCube-native resource_risk operator not in Partura's own EXT set. `acceptable` first calls the ORIGINAL `_acceptable` (so banned_substructures/is_valid_root still apply), then for the 'steer' arm only: dedups equivalent rewrites via `G.dedup_key`+a `first_form` dict (keeping only the first-seen spelling of each canonical form), rejects via `G.banned(e)`, requires at least one of a MUST-keyword set to appear (textual regex over the repr), and finally calls `G.accept(e, u=self._rng.random())` -- this LAST call consumes one extra rng.random() per candidate that reaches it, only when the steer arm's hook is active.

facts.topic: idea_search.py quirk: EXT set construction is vestigial
facts.detail: `EXT = {getattr(f, '__name__', str(f)) for f in getattr(ops_ext, 'NEW_OPERATORS', ())}` treats NEW_OPERATORS entries as if they might be function objects, but ops_ext.NEW_OPERATORS is already a tuple of plain strings -- `getattr('day_flat_ratio', '__name__', str('day_flat_ratio'))` just falls through to `str(f)==f`, so EXT ends up identical to set(NEW_OPERATORS), only via a convoluted path. Harmless today, but worth knowing it is not doing anything clever.

insertion_points.change: Add the same `self.acceptable(child)` check the other 4 mutators already use, in place of (or in addition to) the bare `is_valid_root(child)` check.
insertion_points.risk: This is a behavior change for any run that uses banned_substructures + rolling_block/--ban today: previously-accepted mutated children that happen to still carry a banned structure will now be rejected (fewer accepted mutations per generation, generator.py falls through to generate() more often) -- it changes which trees enter later generations even though it does NOT touch RNG consumption order (acceptable() itself draws no randomness). Should ship with a regression test built on the already-demonstrated repro (ban a real one-layer key, construct a tree with an unrelated mutable window/constant, assert the fix rejects what the old code accepted).

insertion_points.change: Add an optional per-operator weight function (e.g. constructor kwarg `pick_weight: Optional[Callable[[OpSpec], float]] = None`), used only when non-None.
insertion_points.risk: MUST branch so that when no weight function is supplied, the code takes the EXACT original path (`self._rng.choice(sorted(faces))` then `self._rng.choice(faces[face])`), never `self._rng.choices(...)` -- confirmed empirically that `.choice` and `.choices` consume a different number of words from the shared Mersenne Twister state even with uniform weights, so using `.choices` unconditionally (as Partura's own idea_search.py patch does) silently breaks the 'no new params -> identical RNG stream' contract. Also note the 4 call sites pass different candidate pools (e.g. the generate() fallback at line 125 vs the main path at 308-310) -- a weight function keyed by operator name applies uniformly, but testers should exercise all 4 call sites, not just the common one.

insertion_points.where: src/alphacube/mining/generator.py:107-111 (acceptable) plus a new constructor hook
insertion_points.change: Add an optional `accept_hook: Optional[Callable[[Expression], bool]] = None` ANDed into acceptable()'s return, called at the same point as the banned_substructures check, after is_valid_root.
insertion_points.risk: A hook is free to consume self._rng internally (Partura's own G.accept(e, u=self._rng.random()) does exactly this) -- that is fine and expected WHEN a hook is actually installed, but the default (hook=None) path must short-circuit before calling anything, via `hook is None or hook(tree)`, so zero extra rng draws happen when the feature is unused. Also decide whether the hook sees the tree before or after the banned_substructures check (today's idea_search.py calls the original _acceptable first, i.e. ban wins over the custom hook -- a reasonable default to keep).

insertion_points.change: Replace the hardcoded if/else in make_scorer with a dict-based registry (kind -> factory callable) plus a `register_scorer(kind, factory)` function living in scoring.py; have gp.py import and use scoring.FITNESS_KINDS (or a `registered_kinds()` accessor) instead of keeping its own separate tuple, and have GPMiner's fitness_kind validation (gp.py:307-308) defer to the registry instead of a static tuple.
insertion_points.risk: Two independent hardcoded tuples exist today (confirmed via id() to be different objects) plus a THIRD in cli.py's argparse choices= -- missing any one of the three when adding a registry will silently leave a stale validation path. Also: make_scorer's existing kwargs (turnover_penalty, signed, cost_per_side, top_frac, min_coverage, min_scored_days) are forwarded POSITIONALLY/by-name to whichever class is chosen; a generic registry should forward via **kwargs so a plugin factory can pick only what it needs (exactly the pattern Partura's own ParturaScorer(target, **kw) already relies on).

insertion_points.change: To let a scorer factory receive the view's dates (for self-managed train/valid splitting), make_scorer's call sites (gp.py and pipeline.py, both already have `view`/`self.view` in scope) need to pass `dates=view.dates`; make_scorer needs to accept and forward it.

LongHitScorer's **kw forwards straight into LongScorer.__init__, so it would break too. Must add an (initially-ignored) `dates=None` parameter to all three, OR only forward `dates` to kinds registered through the NEW plugin path (never to the 4 built-in kinds), OR introspect the factory's signature before deciding whether to pass it. Whichever is chosen, it is a breaking-signature change to 3 existing classes that several tests construct directly (test_long_scorer.py, test_long_hit_scorer.py) -- those call sites would need no change only if the new parameter is optional and placed where positional callers are unaffected (all 3 use keyword-only args after `target`, so adding another keyword-only default-None arg is safe for existing callers).

insertion_points.where: src/alphacube/cli.py:108-109 (top of cmd_mine) + a new `--plugin` argparse argument
insertion_points.change: Add `--plugin` (action='append', importlib.import_module each value) as the very first statement executed inside cmd_mine, before the `if a.ban_archive:` block (lines 133-138) and before run_mining is called.

A plugin-registered fitness kind will be rejected by argparse before cmd_mine's plugin-loading line ever executes. Decide explicitly whether to (a) drop choices= on --fitness and validate against the live registry inside cmd_mine/run_mining instead, or (b) pre-scan sys.argv for --plugin and import it before build_parser().parse_args() runs in main(). Also decide whether --plugin belongs on the shared `common` parser (benefits research/calculate too, which also call default_registry() indirectly via parser.parse) or only on `mine`'s subparser (smaller, matches the literal ask) -- open question, not decided here.

Checking wall-clock time consumes no RNG, so this is otherwise low-risk for reproducibility.

open_questions: Exactly which 9 of Partura's ops_ext.py operators the registry's boolean/trivial_boolean probe would flag absent ops_ext's own blanket-clearing patch was not independently re-derived -- I confirmed 45 total new operators and 10 '*_ratio'-named ones (one off from the brief's '9'), and confirmed the mechanism is real (in_sustain_stddev is empirically boolean_output=True, trivial_boolean=True in the native registry), but did not run the raw _probe_distinct_values/_probe_constant_capable helpers against each of the 45 kernels individually to get the exact flagged subset.

Whether --plugin should be added to the shared `common` argparse parser (so `research`/`calculate` also get plugin-registered operators, since both reach default_registry() indirectly via parser.parse) or only to the `mine` subparser -- not decided; both are reasonable, the brief's literal wording only mentions the mine path.

Whether the --fitness CLI flag's static argparse choices= should simply be dropped in favor of post-parse validation against the live registry, or whether --plugin loading should move earlier (a sys.argv pre-scan before build_parser().parse_args() in main()) -- this is a real design fork, not just an implementation detail, since it changes where/how argparse errors surface.
