The MODE_P operand path is still the one an implementer will skip, and minimal-diff's narrative about it is inverted. Measured: `div(day_sum(Amt), FloatCap)` plans `S[1] -> P[1]` with the `div` in MODE_P, so the TURNOVER factor -- the headline example -- is precisely the one that raises `RuntimeError: panel operand DF:FloatCap unavailable` without the `_run_panel_round.operand` branch. `_load_leaf_cube` alone makes only the `mul(Ret, LimitWidth)` / `day_mean(...)` family work. Anyone reading minimal-diff's WP4 ordering, its R1, or its test rationale ('a test suite built around the turnover example passes') will patch the wrong one first. Mitigated by two explicit round-structure assertions in WP4's tests, but the brief's own example is the trap.

`board_limit`'s board rules are symbol-format dependent and the default test fixture is the WRONG format, so all three designs' claim that LimitWidth and BoardCode are 'derived, exact, need no build step and are testable on the synthetic cube' is false as written. Measured: on `SH.600000` (synthetic.py:78, hence tests/conftest.py) every rule misses and `board_limit` returns a uniform 0.10 plane; on `600000.SH` (tests/test_tradability.py:11) and on bare `600000` the rules fire. So a test comparing `derive('LimitWidth')` to `board_limit().T` on the conftest store compares two constant planes. Worse: if the production store uses a prefix format, LimitWidth ships as a constant and BoardCode as one category at 100% finite coverage, and no coverage floor catches it. Three-part fix in WP2/WP3/WP9 (assert a rule fires, change the fixture spelling, print both symbol samples before building) -- but the production store's actual format is UNVERIFIED, because I could not reach the server. Check it before WP9 runs.

The symbol-format assumption in the build inherits zero test coverage. `scripts/tearsheet.py:40-58 load_caps` maps `df['symbol']` straight onto the store's symbol list with `.map(col)`, which implies the formats match in the one place this is already done -- but grep confirms that function has no test anywhere, and a mismatch NaNs every cell so the factor scores as low-coverage rather than as broken. The coverage floor in the build script is the only defence, and it is a defence in a script rather than in the type system.

Masking the daily plane by tradability is a judgement call with a visible cost. I mask, for consistency with every other leaf (including `_leaf_panel`'s existing Constant branch) and because the engine is built to stop a fake finite value reaching a suspended stock-day. The consequence: `ts_delta(FloatCap, 5)` is NaN across a suspension even though the cap is perfectly well known on a suspended day, and `LimitWidth` / `BoardCode` -- which are structural, not market data -- are NaN there too. There is no forward-fill operator on the day axis to repair it. The opposite choice leaks finite values into suspended cells, which is worse, but research will feel this one.

float32 and a 1e12 magnitude. Market cap in yuan is 1e9-1e13 and float32 carries ~7 decimal digits, so a 1e12 cap is quantised to ~1e5 yuan. Ranks and ratios are unaffected (~6e-8 relative), but `ts_delta(FloatCap, 1)` differences two nearly-equal large numbers: the day-over-day change is ~1e-3 relative against ~6e-8 of representation noise, so it survives at one horizon and will not at a short enough one. Mitigated rather than solved: the stored planes are float64 on disk, the `Log*` fields are derived in float64 before the cast, and the test asserts the recovery. A researcher who writes `ts_delta(FloatCap, 1)` instead of `ts_delta(LogFloatCap, 1)` still walks into it; nothing stops them.

`is_valid_root` admitting pure-daily roots makes `cs_rank(FloatCap)` a legal factor, and it will score respectably against almost any label because it is a size factor, not alpha. Nothing in this design stops that. It becomes dangerous only once `daily_fields` / `leaf_slots` are switched on, at which point the search finds it immediately. The existing defences (rank-similarity ban, archive dedup, Partura's MUST-neighbourhood) do apply, but all three have to be switched on deliberately, and `daily_leaf_prob > 0` without them is a measurably bad idea.

`ListAge` is wrong at the left edge by construction. A stock listed before the store's first date has no listing date in the data, so I use the 10000 sentinel that Partura's `cross_age` already uses. `is_gt(ListAge, 250)` then treats every old stock as eligible, which is intended, but `div(ListAge, 250)` or `cs_rank(ListAge)` sees a 10000 outlier and is garbage. The sentinel is self-consistent and conventional, and it is a trap for any arithmetic use of the field.

A daily store narrower than the cube makes the warm-up silently empty rather than short. `view.daily()` aligns on `view.dates`, which `warmed_view` has already extended backwards, so uncovered padding rows come back NaN and `ts_mean(FloatCap, 60)` is NaN for the first 60 days of the EVALUATED range, not just the padding. `max_window` sizes the warm-up correctly; there is simply no data there. `resolve` warns when a field's first finite date is after the view's first date and the build script defaults to the cube's full date range, but nothing enforces either.

The exemplar-cache fingerprint does not cover the DERIVED fields when no daily store is attached. `dailyfields.fingerprint` returns None in that case, which is what keeps `view_cache_key` byte-identical for every existing run -- but it means a run using only `LimitWidth` / `BoardCode` / `ListAge`, with no `--daily-fields` directory, keeps the old cache key, so a change to `derive()` would serve stale rank fingerprints. `DERIVED_VERSION` exists and is mixed in only on the attached path. The alternative (always mixing it in) breaks byte-identity for every existing cache directory on disk. Accepted: a change to `derive()` must be paired with clearing the exemplar cache, which is an operational rule, not a mechanism -- the same class of defect typed-correctness was criticised for leaving in place, kept here only for the narrower derived-only case.

`DailyFieldStore` is read through `np.load(mmap_mode='r')` with no guard against a directory someone rebuilt underneath a running process. The build script's temp-dir-then-rename makes a half-built directory unopenable, but it does not stop a long GP run from holding a mapping of a file that has since been replaced. On Linux the old inode survives, so the run stays self-consistent and its `contract_hash` still names the old meta; on a filesystem without that guarantee it would not. Not tested, and not worth a lock for a directory built once.

Eleven work packages over four tightly coupled files (`catalog.py`, `expression.py`, `store.py`, `engine.py`) is a lot of sequencing for an AlphaCube diff of roughly 400 lines plus a 180-line build script. The file-exclusivity constraint drives the count: `catalog.py` ends up owned by the registry package even though half its edit belongs to the daily-field feature, and `conftest.py` is pulled into WP3 only because the fixture's symbol spelling has to change with `synthetic.py`. If one person builds this, WP1-WP4 should be one commit and the dependency graph is better read as a merge order than as a parallelisation plan.

steps: Add keywords to TypedTreeGenerator.__init__: `op_weight=None`, `accept=None`, `daily_fields=()`, `daily_leaf_prob=0.0`, `leaf_slots=None`, `on_exhausted="fallback"`, `mutation_checks_bans=True`. Document at hook_rng that an accept hook MUST draw from it, never from gen._rng: Partura's current hook does `G.accept(e, u=self._rng.random())`, which makes the trajectory depend on how many candidates were thinned and is why its steer/control comparison is not reproducible from the seed.

CONSTRUCTION-TIME VALIDATION: every op_weight key names a registered operator; every value is a finite float >= 0; accept is callable with exactly one positional parameter; and `[s for s in self.specs if s.reduces_m and not s.non_root]` is non-empty after dropping weight-0 operators (measured at 26 specs -- emptying it makes generate()'s fallback reach `self._rng.choice(sorted({}))` -> IndexError and _gen('daily', 1, ...) raise ShapeError forever). Raise ValueError naming the cause.

Factor the ban check out: `def _ban_ok(self, tree): return not (self.banned_substructures and (self.banned_substructures & one_layer_keys(tree)))`. `acceptable` becomes is_valid_root -> _ban_ok -> `self.accept_hook is None or bool(self.accept_hook(tree))`, in that order, keeping the short-circuit so one_layer_keys is computed only when a ban set exists.

FIX generate()'s fallback (line 125), which bypasses acceptable() entirely -- measured: an always-False acceptable still returns day_cov(Close, Volume), and generate_population(8) returns 8 unaccepted trees. Keep the first retry loop byte-identical, then: `pool = self._root_ops_of('reduce')`; `tries = 1 if (self.accept_hook is None and not self.banned_substructures) else GENERATE_FALLBACK_TRIES` (module constant 64); loop drawing `self._collapse_leaf(self._pick(pool))`, return the first acceptable one, remembering the first that passes `_ban_ok and is_valid_root` as `relaxed`; if relaxed is None or on_exhausted=='raise', raise a new `GenerationExhausted(ValueError)` naming the ban-set size and whether a hook is installed; otherwise increment unaccepted_fallbacks and return relaxed. With no ban and no hook, tries==1 and the first candidate is always acceptable, so the draws and the result are byte-identical.

`_pick`: build the faces dict as today, then `if self.op_weight is None: return self._rng.choice(faces[self._rng.choice(sorted(faces))])` -- generator.py:274 verbatim, two _randbelow draws in the same order. Only otherwise call `self._pick_weighted(faces)`. (Measured: two `choice`s then random() gives 0.3948..., two `choices` gives 0.6509... -- the paths are not interchangeable.)

`_pick_weighted(faces)`: per face compute `max(0.0, float(self.op_weight(s)))` per spec, drop faces whose total is 0, pick the face with `self._rng.choices(names, weights=[mean weight per face])`, then the operator with `self._rng.choices(ss, weights=ws)`. If every face drops out, fall back to the uniform path. This reproduces Partura's current pick semantics exactly, so the migration is behaviour-preserving.

FIX `mutate_window` (line 234) and `mutate_constant` (line 246): replace the final `is_valid_root(child)` with `self.acceptable(child) if self.mutation_checks_bans else is_valid_root(child)`. The default is the FIX; mutation_checks_bans=False exists only to bit-reproduce an old --ban run. Verified: the full suite is 617/10/1 with the default on.
Leave `mutate_operator` alone -- it already routes through self._pick(alts), so weights reach operator swaps for free.

In `_gen`'s `depth <= 1` branch (line 300-305), between the `req == 'full'` return and the `_collapse_leaf`: `if self.daily_fields and self._rng.random() < self.daily_leaf_prob: return DailyFeature(self._rng.choice(self.daily_fields))`. work_packages.title: Server build script for the stored daily fields
steps: New scripts/build_daily_fields.py. CLI: --store (cube store root, opened read-only purely for its canonical symbols/dates), --cap-dir (default /root/autodl-tmp/qmt_daily_data/daily_capital), --out (default /root/autodl-tmp/AlphaCube/daily_fields), --only FIELD (repeatable), --min-coverage (default 0.5), --dry-run.
REFUSE to run if --out resolves inside --cap-dir or inside the store directory. The source data directories are never written to.

Probe one parquet's schema first and print its columns. Then PRINT THE STORE'S FIRST 10 SYMBOLS NEXT TO THE PARQUET'S FIRST 10 `symbol` VALUES -- this is the only visible defence against the format mismatch that NaNs every cell, and scripts/tearsheet.py's load_caps (which maps df['symbol'] straight onto the store's symbol list) has zero test coverage.

Read `symbol`, `circulating_market_value`, `total_market_value` (the exact names load_caps already uses, scripts/tearsheet.py:52) plus a share column if one exists; record which column fed which field in meta.json's `columns_used`.

For each field build an (S, D) FLOAT64 plane over the store's own symbols/dates, NaN where a date file is missing or a symbol is absent that day. One parquet read per date, streamed -- never hold more than one day's frame.

Write FloatShares ONLY if a real share column exists. Never synthesise it from FloatCap / Close: Close is back-adjusted while Amt/Volume are raw, so the ratio would not be a share count. Write NO Log* plane -- dailyfields.resolve derives those in float64 from the stored plane.

Write daily_<name>.npy per field and meta.json with fields, n_symbols, n_days, symbols, dates, source paths, built_at, columns_used, per-field finite coverage and the first/last date with any data. Write into a temp directory under --out's parent and os.replace it into place, so a half-built directory is never readable.
Exit non-zero when any built field's finite coverage is below --min-coverage, printing the per-field numbers. This is the failure mode that otherwise produces a silently empty factor.
Print the DERIVED and LOG field names at the end with a note that they need no build step, so the operator does not look for files that will never exist.
tests: tests/test_build_daily_fields.py: against a hand-written parquet directory (3 dates x 4 symbols, one date missing, one symbol absent on one date) the planes are (S, D) float64, NaN exactly where expected, meta.json records columns_used and per-field coverage, and the output is immediately readable by DailyFieldStore
